abandon: The mechanism says on-policy RL settles on the change nearest the base in KL that raises reward, and that on math text this nearest change is the same for the Math and Code rewards, so the two deltas flip the same MATH-500 items. result-edceef tests this directly on a second Olmo pair: same base, on-policy RL, Math reward vs Code reward. The two do not come out the same. Its words: "in the Olmo 3 RL-Zero models the MATH-500 gain follows the math share of the reward; IF and Code RL give none". The figures are "Math 3.0 448 (+7.6 pts [4.2, 11.0])" against "Code 3.0 411 (+0.2 [-3.4, 3.8])", and the prediction that the mechanism needs is marked failed: "R3 (Code 3.0 = Math 3.0) refuted". Code 3.0 gains nothing over the cued base (410), so it cannot flip the problems Math 3.0 fixes. The same item adds that the Code effect seen in result-4b0d5f ("Code-RL: plain 390, cue 450") "holds for the 3.1 Code release only, though Code 3.0 moved the weights further (relative norm 0.151 % vs 0.109 %)". Code 3.0 is not just a smaller step toward the same change: it moved the weights further than Code 3.1 and still produced no math gain. So the math gain depends on the release, not on a KL-nearest math change shared by every reward. The Code 3.1 / Math 3.1 match in result-4b0d5f and result-e45bf4 ("Code-RL = theta0.5 (-0.9 [-5.5,3.7])") is a matching total score for one release. RL's Razor does not explain it, because the same reasoning would predict the same match for Code 3.0. Also, result-9b6af3 shows that matching totals say little at the item level: "the random cell (a fresh base sample in effect) gets 42 of the cued base's 90 wrong problems right". A kappa test of shared flips would therefore start from a high noise floor.
